problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=Z\times Z$ in the Cartesian plane?
worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S=Z\times Z
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is an integer number and whose $y$-coordinate is an integer number.

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in Z,\,y\in Z}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{-1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $-1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any integer number.

$$
{S}_{-1}={(-1,y)\,:\,y\in Z}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{-1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/9673951b4e72ba503e740369462f9e528e43ffc083706ee558ade7ccd52702f5.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{0}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $0$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any integer number.

$$
{S}_{0}={(0,y)\,:\,y\in Z}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{0}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/797b66a293eb241f841869abe97e324f4301907f71029acceefd68487bef1b4f.png)

We can create the subsets $…,{S}_{-3},{S}_{-2},{S}_{1},{S}_{2},{S}_{3},…$ similarly. Our Cartesian product $S$ is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =…\cup {S}_{-3}\cup {S}_{-2}\cup {S}_{-1}\cup {S}_{0}\cup {S}_{1}\cup \text{ }{S}_{2}\cup {S}_{3}… \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in Z}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize $Z\times Z$ as the set of points in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/de19fcf0f246b09d4bb957568e026b36de3f55c1a6c7065d79faacee794a8326.png)
